concepts.title: Subject-Verb Agreement: Fill the Blank
concepts.definition: A singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb. Words like each, every, neither, either and news stay singular; the real subject may sit away from the verb inside a of-phrase.
concepts.formula: one subject -> singular verb;  two subjects joined by and -> plural verb
concepts.key_idea: Find the true subject first; ignore the noun inside 'of ...'.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the verb that agrees with the subject
Choose is or are, has or have for the sentence
Complete the sentence so the verb agrees

solution_steps.explain: the noun inside 'of ...' is never the subject
each, every, neither, either, news, mathematics are singular
singular subject -> is/has/verb-s; plural subject -> are/have/base verb

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: The list of items ___ on the desk. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: My friends ___ football after school. (play)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Each of the boys ___ a pen. (have)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: The news ___ very good today. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Neither of the answers ___ correct. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Ravi and his sister ___ to the same school. (go)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject. (be)

concepts.title: Prepositions of Time and Place
concepts.definition: Prepositions link a noun to the rest of the sentence. In is used for months, years and inside spaces; on for days, dates and surfaces; at for clock times and points; since and across follow fixed senses.
concepts.formula: in July, on Monday, at 5 o'clock, since Monday
concepts.key_idea: Time words decide in, on, at: month or year - in; day or date - on; clock time - at.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition
Choose in, on or at for the sentence
Complete the sentence with a preposition

solution_steps.explain: month/year -> in; day/date/surface -> on; clock time -> at
inside a space -> in; a surface or line -> on; a point -> at

Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: She has been unwell ___ Monday.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The library is ___ the second floor.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He walked ___ the road carefully.

concepts.title: Comparatives and Superlatives: One Word
concepts.definition: Short adjectives add -er and -est; adjectives ending in a consonant + y change y to ier and iest; long adjectives take more and most. A few adjectives are irregular: good-better-best, bad-worse-worst.
concepts.key_idea: Syllables decide: one syllable takes -er/-est, long words take more/most.
question_patterns: Write the comparative or superlative form of the adjective
Give the -er or -est form of the word
